## LANDED and CLOSED — final state

**Change 1657** — `LLM-Review +1`, `Verified +1`, submitted and **MERGED** 2026-08-12 11:51:15,
landing on Gerrit `main` as **`cc69cc1179`** (Gerrit rebased server-side on submit, so the local
pre-rebase sha `037230e756` is not the landed one). Closed `--class preexisting`: the
terminal-and-lossy budget had been there since the lock was written — 7084 changed hold DURATION,
never this failure SHAPE.

Note for anyone verifying: at close time `origin/main` (the GitHub mirror) had **not** yet
replicated the merge, so a `git merge --ff-only origin/main` aborts and a trailer search against
`origin/main` finds nothing. The merge is real — confirmed directly against the `gerrit` remote,
where `cc69cc1179` carries the `rebar-ticket:` trailer and `write_path_retries` is present in
`lock.py`. This is mirror lag, not a failed submit.

### All 20 acceptance criteria verified against the merged tree

Opted-in sites exactly 3/1/1 and the advisory push merge fail-fast (AST test); reproduction
RED/GREEN; docs carry both the ~180s ceiling and `REBAR_LOCK_RETRIES`; `lock.py` 798 lines vs the
800 cap; `retries` default 0 on both `acquire` and `write_lock`. `make lint` and `make typecheck`
clean; 5320 unit tests pass.

### One defect the full suite caught that would otherwise have shipped

`docs/env-vars.md` is GENERATED, and its drift gate failed. Regenerating was not enough: the
generator resolves only string-LITERAL keys, so `os.environ.get(_RETRY_ENV_VAR)` registered as
`<non-literal>` and the new variable would have shipped **undocumented** — exactly what that
registry exists to prevent. Fixed by inlining the literal, with a comment recording why it is not
a constant. Worth knowing for anyone adding an env var.

### Discovered work, filed and linked `discovered_from` (all open)

* `larval-tribal-tigermoth` — stale mkdir lock UNBOUNDED without `/proc`: the recycled-pid branch
  at `lock.py:555-560` has no discriminator (`_process_start_time()` is always `None`) and is
  exempt from the 1h ceiling. Explains the observed 12-minute dead-holder wedge. NOT an fd leak
  and NOT `start=-` — both conclusively ruled out.
* `silvern-dewy-damselfly` — `transition` close reports a lock error with **exit 0** after the
  close landed, silently downgrading to closed-without-signature. This change MITIGATES it (the
  signature append is now on a retrying path) but does not fix the reporting shape.
* `inborn-asbestine-moray` — `sign-review` advertises a no-LLM recovery that cannot work when the
  same contention episode took the sidecar too.

### Residual risk to hand on

`lock.py` sits at **798 of 800** lines. The retry cluster was kept in place rather than extracted
because it is well under the 100-LOC floor the module-size policy sets for a new file — but the
next edit to this module will need a real split along a call-graph seam, not a trim.
